configuration: the upstream ctest entry hoctests::test_legacy_setpointer_py: run the shipped script unchanged; run.sh extracts the first two numeric fields of the two lines naming soma(0.5) into stdout_values.txt (the script also prints expected-error text containing digits, which anchoring skips)
observable: the four values on the script's two soma(0.5) output lines, extracted into stdout_values.txt
variant: identical to nominal, with reason: the shipped script constructs its whole model and inputs itself and seeds any random stream it uses, so no external initial condition reaches it; an identical copy is the only sensible variant and the tolerance is exercised by the altbuild floor
altbuild: an -O0 build of the same source: run.sh altbuild appends -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-O0 and -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-O0 to the same cmake flags and builds into its own cache entry; selfcheck runs the nominal inputs on it and measures this check's floor from the disagreement between the two builds

evidence.floor_how: measured at selfcheck: the largest per-value disagreement between the nominal run and the altbuild run (an -O0 build of the same source), recorded in self-validation.json and copied here at calibration

warrant: Upstream grades this hoctests entry by the process exit status alone; the run still computes real numeric results, so the honest strengthening is to grade those values pointwise while keeping the upstream process (and its internal assertions) intact. The band is achievable because the run is deterministic and single-threaded; repeats agree bit for bit and the -O0 altbuild moves the four values only at the measured floor. It is discriminating because a real fault in pointer wiring between mechanisms changes the printed values far outside the band. The floor is measured against the declared -O0 altbuild at selfcheck.
